info.title: Polymorfa Console & Management API
info.description:
Complete console/management surface. Resource-oriented REST: `{param}` path variables, single-word action sub-resources.

Namespaces decide inclusion:
- `/platform/…` — **public registry** (283 endpoints): each endpoint declares either a scoped `pmfa_` team key or a verified live dashboard JWT, or dashboard-only authorization when a specific user's authority is required. Only implemented handlers are published to customers and SDKs.
- `/console/…` — **console-only** (130 endpoints): verified dashboard identity. EXCLUDED from the published spec; reason per endpoint.

The published customer spec = this document filtered to `x-audience: public` endpoints with an implemented runtime handler.
Most transitional body/response schemas remain loose (`additionalProperties: true`); session-control operations use explicit strict schemas.

get.description:
**Required scope:** `events:listen`

Opens a server-sent event (SSE) stream of this project's events. Every event frame carries the same event object as the events API and the exact webhook body when it is available.

Send `Accept: text/event-stream`. Resume after a disconnect by sending the last received `cursor` as `Last-Event-ID` or `cursor`. Cursors are valid for 24 hours and are bound to the team, project and `types` filter.

With `ack=auto` (default), each event is released as soon as it is written. With `ack=manual`, at most `maxInFlight` events are outstanding until you acknowledge them; unacknowledged events produce a `backpressure` frame and then a `dropped` frame.

The stream sends a `heartbeat` frame every `heartbeatIntervalMs`. It closes with `revoked` within one heartbeat after the credential, project or feature access ends, and with `expiry` at `connectionExpiresAt` or after `idleTimeoutMs` without an event. Reconnect from the last cursor after `expiry`, `dropped` or a recoverable `gap`.

Requires `events:listen` and the Event streams beta. Team keys and project tokens are accepted; client tokens are rejected.

schema.description: Comma-separated event types to include, or repeat the parameter. A trailing `*` matches a prefix, such as `message.*`. Omit for every type. At most 32 filters.
Resume after this cursor. Equivalent to `Last-Event-ID`; if both are sent they must match.
`auto` (default) releases events once written. `manual` holds them until acknowledged.
Resume cursor sent automatically by SSE clients after a reconnect.

200.description: An SSE stream. The first frame is `ready`. `revoked`, `expiry`, `dropped` and `gap` frames end the connection, except a `gap` with reason `retention_exceeded`, which reports skipped events and the stream continues.

400.description: Invalid parameter, or `stream_cursor_invalid` when the cursor belongs to another project or filter.

403.description: `missing_scope`, `permission_denied`, or `feature_unavailable` when Event streams is not enabled for the team.

error.message: The resume cursor is older than the stream retention window.

On an unlaunched draft, a new `senderConfig` passes the same checks as create and plans are checked at launch. Once the campaign has launched, including a scheduled launch that has not started, a new `senderConfig` passes the launch checks and can answer `402 campaigns_not_entitled` or `400 invalid_parameter`. `recipientListId` points the campaign at another audience while it is still an unlaunched draft and replaces its existing recipients; after launch it answers `409`. `templateId`, `variableMapping`, `messagesArray` and `composerBlueprint` also change only while the campaign is an unlaunched draft; after launch a different value answers `409`, and the stored value is accepted. Aggregated number activity and operational vitals. Returns disabled with null summary and empty data until a team owner or admin enables Analytics. Conversation rates use completed 24-hour direct-chat cohorts, booked in the period when they mature; missing or dropped cohort coverage returns null rates. Read means an observed read receipt, not a verified app open. No contact identifiers or message content. Linked Devices telemetry only; unsupported or unobserved numbers carry measured=false. Bucket timestamps use UTC. Activity series use hourly buckets for ranges up to 48 hours and daily buckets for longer ranges. Call series use daily buckets. Message metadata compares direct sends and completed conversations by type, coarse text/caption length, source, calling code and observed device count. Device observations are bounded samples. Calling-code shares describe conversations, not distinct people or location. Presence signals require existing subscriptions. Primary phone activity spans end at their last observed signal and close after 15 minutes without evidence. Quiet gaps end at the next observed signal. Duration sums and averages count completed intervals and exclude open or restart-censored intervals; they do not measure phone online/offline or power state. Metadata collection uses the current team opt-in; disable erases these aggregates and stale queued metadata is rejected. Calls aggregate retained records by their immutable original number/project ownership, including supported Official API calls; message measured/coverage fields do not apply to calls. Call series groups starts by UTC day. Answer rate excludes still-ringing calls; timing fields have explicit observation counts. Missed-call follow-up observes an answered outgoing call to the same pseudonymous contact within 24h, including after the requested end; only completed windows with a known contact form the denominator. It does not prove callback intent. Quality uses reported measurements, latest cumulative app reports per connection and per-call averages. Breakdown counts can overlap. Disabling hides this call view without deleting operational call history. Device analytics estimates sending client families from message ID prefixes, not verified hardware. Customer/account distributions count observed live direct messages, not unique people or installed devices; unknown is included. Older retained buckets lack device coverage and return null shares. Each number exposes at most 25 of its own device indexes, coarse reported class and last observed sending activity. A list change makes inventory membership/count unknown until another full list. Inventory is null in the combined summary. No recipient device identity or raw message ID is retained by this analytics block. Joint conversation breakdown rows retain first outgoing message type, length band, send source, inferred calling code and observed customer device-count class together with UTC completion bucket. Combine rows matching all selected categories to drill into countries and message attributes without inferring intersections from independent marginal totals. Calling codes do not establish current location and shared codes do not identify a unique country. Counts describe completed 24-hour conversation cohorts, not distinct customers. Rates and averages are null when coverage is missing, dropped or truncated. At most 4096 number/time/category groups are returned in one scope, prioritizing largest groups and marking truncation; raw reply latency sums support weighted aggregation. Connection/call vitals and live message platform distributions are separate measurements, not recipient-country filtered cohorts. Recipient country and recipient linked-device-count fields refine joint conversation metadata. Recipient activity remains hourly even for long date ranges, supporting incoming-message timing in an explicit time zone. Delivery signals do not prove reading; read signals are distinct. Presence subscriptions are best-effort around permitted direct sends, reuse a live bounded local lease, preserve observation-off policies and never poll every contact. Missing presence is Unknown, not offline.
